n1.speaker: narrator
n1.text: The rains came and went. With water in the ground again, the herds did what herds do.

n2.speaker: tendai
n2.text: Look at them, {player}. Impala from fence to fence. A year ago I would have wept for joy.

n3.speaker: tendai
n3.text: Now look at the grass. You can see the ground through it.

n4.speaker: narrator
n4.text: A dusty car rattles up to the gate. A woman climbs out with a clipboard, binoculars and a sun hat that has seen better decades.

n5.speaker: amara
n5.text: Dr. Amara Okafor. I wrote to you. I have been counting your impala from the road for the last ten kilometres.

n6.speaker: amara
n6.text: I lost count somewhere after a hundred and twenty.

choices.text: Welcome. We could use the help.

help.speaker: amara
help.text: Good. Then we start with numbers, not feelings.

bad.speaker: amara
bad.text: On land this size, with grass this thin? It is a lot. Let us count properly before anyone panics.

count.speaker: amara
count.text: Tomorrow at first light, we count. Every herd. Then we decide what to do.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Dawn. Amara walks the plains with a tally counter in each hand.

n1.speaker: amara
n1.text: Click on a herd and you will see what I see: how many there are, how many the land can feed, and why the number moved yesterday.

n2.speaker: amara
n2.text: The plains can feed maybe eighty impala right now. You have far more. Some will starve, and they will take the grass down with them.

n3.speaker: tendai
n3.text: The lions and the hyenas take their share. They always have.

n4.speaker: amara
n4.text: They do. But a few lions cannot eat their way through a boom this size. Not fast enough to save the grass.

n5.speaker: tendai
n5.text: So it is guns, is it? I spent eight years keeping guns out of this place.

n6.speaker: amara
n6.text: I did not say guns. I said we need a plan. There is more than one kind.

n7.speaker: amara
n7.text: One good thing: my university pays a research grant while I work here. Sixty a day. Spend it on people who can carry out a plan.

n8.speaker: narrator
n8.text: Before anyone can say more, a ranger’s radio crackles. Something about the east fence. Something about elephants.

n9.speaker: tendai
n9.text: That will be the village fields. I will go and look. You had better come too, tomorrow.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: By noon there is a crowd at the main gate.

n1.speaker: narrator
n1.text: At the front stands a tall woman in a bright headwrap, arms folded.

n2.speaker: wanjiru
n2.text: You are Ruth’s grandchild. I am Wanjiru. I speak for the village on your eastern side.

n3.speaker: wanjiru
n3.text: Last night your elephants walked through your fence and ate half a season of maize. Three families’ fields. Gone.

n4.speaker: wanjiru
n4.text: When Ruth was alive, we had an understanding. Since she died, nobody answers for anything that comes out of this reserve.

choices.text: I’m sorry. We will make this right.
Elephants are wild animals. We can’t control them.

sorry.speaker: wanjiru
sorry.text: Sorry fills no granary. But it is a start.

wild.speaker: wanjiru
wild.text: Then why keep them behind a fence at all? Either they are yours, or they are not.

ruth.speaker: wanjiru
ruth.text: She mended fences. She gave our young people work. And when her animals ate our crops, she paid. Every time.

end.speaker: wanjiru
end.text: Come to the village when you have a real answer. I will not come to this gate twice.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: That evening the office is crowded. Tendai leans by the door, Amara spreads maps across Ruth’s desk.

n1.speaker: amara
n1.text: Two problems. The impala are eating the plains bare, and the elephants are leaving to eat the village. They are connected: hungry elephants wander.

n2.speaker: amara
n2.text: For the impala, I would cull. Quickly, properly, and the meat goes to the village. It is what the numbers say.

n3.speaker: tendai
n3.text: Numbers. Ruth never shot an animal in thirty years.

n4.speaker: tendai
n4.text: Move them. There are reserves up north that would take impala. Or let the predators do their work, and give it time.

n5.speaker: amara
n5.text: Moving animals costs money and needs a vet. Contraception is slow, but it is kind. Culling is fast. It is not kind.

n6.speaker: amara
n6.text: It is your reserve, {player}. Whatever you choose, I will help you do it well.

choices.text: We cull. The meat goes to the village.
We relocate them. We find them a new home.
Contraception. Slow, but we do no harm.

cull.speaker: tendai
cull.text: Then do it quietly, and do it once.

n9.speaker: narrator
n9.text: Hire a culling team (Staff, H), then click the impala and press Cull. Each press lowers the target by ten.

relocate.speaker: amara
relocate.text: Then hire a vet and start saving. Every animal we move costs money.

n11.speaker: narrator
n11.text: Hire a vet (Staff, H), then click the impala and press Relocate. Each press lowers the target by ten.

contra.speaker: amara
contra.text: It will take a season to show. The grass will have to hold out until then.

n13.speaker: narrator
n13.text: Hire a vet (Staff, H), then click the impala and press Contraception. Fewer calves are born while it runs.

end.speaker: tendai
end.text: And the village? Wanjiru will not wait long.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The next morning you walk the east road to the village. Wanjiru meets you at the edge of the trampled fields.

n1.speaker: wanjiru
n1.text: Well? What is the real answer?

choices.text: A beehive fence along the elephants’ path, built with your beekeepers.
When our elephants take your crops, the reserve pays. Every time.
We will mend the fence properly. That should hold them.

bees.speaker: wanjiru
bees.text: Bees! That was Ruth’s idea too, before the money ran out. Elephants hate them. And the honey sells.

n4.speaker: narrator
n4.text: Build the beehive fence on its marked spot at the east edge of the plains (Build, B).

pay.speaker: wanjiru
pay.text: Paid. Every time. I will hold you to that.

n6.speaker: narrator
n6.text: From now on, each raid costs money instead of most of the village’s trust.

fence.speaker: wanjiru
fence.text: Ruth mended that fence a hundred times. The elephants knocked it down a hundred and one.

n8.speaker: narrator
n8.text: A mended fence slows the raids, but elephants can still break it.

end.speaker: wanjiru
end.text: Then we will see. My people are watching what you do, not what you say.

n10.speaker: tendai
n10.text: The fence between the plains and the east border is down anyway. Mend it and we can work on this side of the reserve too.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The first log hives hang along the wire. By evening they hum.

n1.speaker: wanjiru
n1.text: My grandson sat under that fence all afternoon, waiting for an elephant to try it. None came.

n2.speaker: tendai
n2.text: Ruth would have laughed until she cried.

start.speaker: tendai
start.text: Amara keeps asking who is going to carry out this plan of yours.

n1.speaker: tendai
n1.text: A cull needs a culling team; moving animals or contraception needs a vet. Hire them from the Staff panel (H), then click the impala.

start.speaker: amara
start.text: That is the target. The impala are down to what the plains can carry.

cull.speaker: tendai
cull.text: I took the meat to the village myself. Wanjiru did not thank me. But she did not send it back either.

relocate.speaker: tendai
relocate.text: The last truck left at dawn. Off to a new home up north. I waved at it like a fool.

contra.speaker: amara
contra.text: Fewer calves this season, and the herd is settling. Slow, but it is working.

end.speaker: amara
end.text: Now the grass has a chance. Give it time, and keep the water up.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The woodland is cool and quiet after the plains. Tendai stops beside a thorn tree.

n1.speaker: tendai
n1.text: Look. A wire snare. New wire, not a spot of rust on it.

n2.speaker: tendai
n2.text: This is not some hungry boy after a meal. Somebody set a whole line of these, right on the game paths.

choices.text: Could it be someone from the village?

organised.speaker: tendai
organised.text: Organised, and paid. We will need more rangers out here.

village.speaker: tendai
village.text: Maybe. But village boys do not buy steel cable by the drum.

end.speaker: tendai
end.text: I will pull these. Keep your eyes open, {player}. This is not finished.

start.speaker: tendai
start.text: The fence between the plains and the east border is still down. Click it to mend it, and the east side of the reserve opens up.

start.speaker: amara
start.text: The grass is slow to come back. A wet season will help, and so will fewer mouths. Click the plains to see how it is doing.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The plains are green at the edges again.

n1.speaker: amara
n1.text: Grass coming back, herds the land can carry, and a village that is still talking to us. That is a good season’s work.

n2.speaker: amara
n2.text: I would like to stay, if you will have me. There is a lot here worth counting.

choices.text: Only if you promise to argue with Tendai less.

team.speaker: amara
team.text: Then I had better find somewhere to sleep that is not the car.

argue.speaker: tendai
argue.text: She will not. But she is usually right, which is worse.

village.speaker: narrator
village.text: A message comes from the village.

ally.speaker: wanjiru
ally.text: My people have stopped saying “your” elephants. Now it is just “the” elephants. That is progress.

wary.speaker: wanjiru
wary.text: The village is watching. Keep your promises and we will keep ours.

next.speaker: tendai
next.text: People in town were asking about the reserve last week. Real tourists, {player}. With cameras.

n10.speaker: tendai
n10.text: Maybe it is time we gave them something to look at.
